title: Hold a spring-open berry clamshell punnet lid flush and slide its front snap catch shut
instruction: Press and hold the spring-open berry clamshell lid flush down onto the base rim with one hand without slamming or crushing the strawberries, slide the front snap catch cleanly home with the other hand to latch it shut, then release both hands clear.
context: Packing fresh berries into hinged clear PET clamshell punnets is a high-volume manual agricultural packinghouse operation (Packers and Packagers, Hand, O*NET 53-7064.00, >600,000 US workers; Graders and Sorters, Agricultural Products, O*NET 45-2041.00). Thermoformed clamshell lids spring open ~24 deg on their living hinge and pop open unless one hand holds the lid perimeter flat without bruising the berries while the other hand engages the front snap catch.
setup: Positions are in cm on the station tabletop (z = TOP = 74.75 cm) from the midpoint between the two YAM arm bases at (0, +/-30.5) cm (x forward, y left, z up). Centered at (27.5, 0.0, TOP) cm sits a 1:1 clear PET hinged strawberry clamshell punnet (16.0 cm wide along y x 12.0 cm deep along x x 6.5 cm tall closed; 525 g total). Base tub (11.2 x 15.2 x 4.3 cm, 4 mm walls/floor, 12.0 x 16.0 x 0.4 cm top rim flange, 460 g) holds a white absorbent liner pad and eight ripe red strawberries with green calyx caps seated below the 4.3 cm rim. Along the rear +x edge (x_local = +5.8 cm, z_local = 4.3 cm) two hinge barrels carry a 40 g clear PET domed lid (16.0 x 12.0 cm overall; central raised berry dome 9.0 x 9.6 x 1.8 cm leaving flat 3.2 cm structural pressing shoulders with blue target pads at y = +/-6.2 cm, plus a 1.0 x 2.0 x 0.5 cm front lock tongue at y = 0). A hinge return spring (rest 26.5 deg, k = 0.55 N*m/rad, damping 0.018 N*m/(rad/s)) holds the lid open at 24.4 deg at start. On the front -x rim rail (x_local = -6.5 cm, z_local = 4.3 cm) sits a 25 g orange sliding snap catch (PrismaticJoint along y) with a forward gripper tab (1.4 x 1.4 x 2.4 cm at x = 19.1 cm) and a green center LOCK mark at y = 0. Arm assignment is randomized left/right via HAND_SIDE=L|R (setup screenshot shows L): the catch starts open 3.2 cm to the latch arm's side (-3.2 cm for L, +3.2 cm for R) and must slide to 0.0 cm.
scoring: Evaluated at episode end (SCORE_OVER = end). Any hazard permanently latches score to 0.0: (1) lid slammed shut (angle <= 15.0 deg with closing velocity < -2.20 rad/s), (2) gripper palm or finger enters the open punnet's central berry cavity (8.8 x 12.8 x 3.0 cm centered at (0, 0, 2.0) cm in base frame while lid > 5.0 deg), or (3) punnet disturbed (tilt > 12.0 deg, |yaw| > 15.0 deg, XY drift > 4.5 cm, or underside < TOP - 1.5 cm). Without hazards: 0.25 if the lid is currently held flush (<= 3.0 deg; drops back to 0.0 if released unlatched and the lid springs open); 0.50 if flush (<= 3.0 deg) and the snap catch is within +/-12 mm of center without jamming; 0.75 if flush (<= 3.0 deg) and the snap catch is locked at center (<= 4.0 mm); 1.0 (success, held 1.0 s / 20 steps at 20 Hz) when the lid stays latched closed (<= 3.0 deg, |vel| <= 0.10 rad/s), the catch stays locked at center (<= 4.0 mm, |vel| <= 0.010 m/s), the punnet rests flat and still on the tabletop (tilt <= 4.0 deg, |low_z - TOP| <= 5 mm, < 5 mm/s, < 5 deg/s), and both grippers are out of contact (> 2 mm) with punnet base, lid, and catch. Real-trial verification: check video for smooth closing and zero berry contact, verify lid closure angle <= 3 deg with a protractor/gage and catch centered within 4 mm after 1.0 s hands-clear release.
reset_notes: Slide the front orange snap catch back 3.2 cm to its open side stop, allow the hinge spring to lift the clear PET lid open to ~24 deg, inspect strawberries and punnet alignment on the tabletop mark, and return both arms to READY.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX with a 525 g punnet base, a rear-hinged lid on a return spring, and a sliding snap catch with a detent and premature-latch jam. Strawberries are rigid geometry in the tub; bruising and lid slam are modelled as berry-cavity intrusion and closing angular-velocity thresholds, not deformable fruit. The thermoformed PET is rigid.
